gossipPool: My friend got marrried and didn’t even invite me. I had the front seat to her wedding preparations, her millennial-coded memes. People she hasn’t talked to for years are at this wedding. And I know the aesthetic she went for, the photographers she hired, the foods she made. Her backyard is still similar to me like it was 13 years ago. If I ask her, she’ll say it’s because I’ve moved countries and we aren’t friends anymore. But I know it’s because we used to talk about love and she can’t let herself been seen with someone she just settled for

My professor that used to teach me Fundamentals of Visual Design on first year was cheating on his wife with his back then, first year student. She (the student) was trying to weasel into an exhibition that me and my best friend were doing (bestie was a curator), but we didn’t want her work – not because it was bad/good, it didn’t fit our idea; she thought that the professor will be able to influence us to get her into the event. Curator did not budge. I graduated few years ago, recently I was informed that because of our resistance, she broke up with him and he didn’t divorce his wife (but I wish the wife would do it lol)

I have a neighbor who is a public servant, once they offered me drugs and I’ve seen him giving packages to strange people late at night. I sort of suspect he sells drugs or is involved in some shady business.

When I worked in urban development, part of my job was to create urban development plans for different municipalities. One of them was in the southern part of the state, and as part of my work, I had to research everything related to the environment.

During my research, I discovered that there was a coke and sulfur storage facility that had been abandoned for years, with no maintenance or any kind of oversight. Whenever it rained, all of that material would seep into the surrounding land and nearby homes. I found reports of crops being lost, animals being affected, and residents reporting cases of leukemia and birth defects. I don't know how much of that had been medically confirmed, but there was definitely a serious environmental problem that needed attention, and there were news articles to back it up.

When I asked what we could do with that information or how we should address it in the development plan, I was told not to mention it. To ignore the whole thing and turn a blind eye.

Then someone said something along the lines of, "Are you crazy? Do you want to get kidnapped or something? Do you want to end up as another missing person on a search poster?"

And well, that's the gossip. There I was, working on an urban development plan, researching the living conditions of a community, and discovering that there were things I simply wasn't allowed to write about because someone didn't want that information getting out.

Recently, I caught wind of some secondhand gossip (someone was telling my friend about it, but I happened to be right there next to her, being nosy and listening to the voice messages).

A friend of mine broke things off with someone he was almost in a relationship with. I thought they made a cute couple, but for the sake of adding a little more gossip, my friend had been single for a really long time before meeting this girl.

Watching the entire life cycle of their relationship made me wonder whether it's okay to have high expectations about what you want from a relationship, or whether relationships are more about sacrificing parts of who you are for the greater good

Anyway, I think they both learned a lot about who they are as people. I hope things go well for them, wherever they decide to go.

In December, I'm going to be the maid of honor at my mother-in-law's 40th wedding anniversary celebration. Years ago, I never would have imagined this happening, especially after she caught me sleeping with her son in his bed. After that incident, she threatened to take legal action to keep me from ever going near her son again.

Today, her son is my husband, and she absolutely adores me.

gossipLore: Gossip was an Atari video game released in the 80’s where users could gossip about the game characters through a virtual telephone. It was created by Chris Crawford, who wanted video games to be a more expressive art form. He called this type of game "people games", and at the time, he was told that this was boring. Many of us who spent more than 5 hours living a second, unhinged life in the Sims beg to differ.

Philosopher Mladen Dolar calls gossip a "source of social bonding and empowerment for all groups that have limited or no access to the public sphere", noting how, in contexts like queer and Black communities, gossip can become a tool of resistance and social cohesion.

The story in the novel "Tropical Night Falling", written by Argentinian writer Manuel Puig, is developed entirely through the gossip of its two main characters: two elderly Argentinian women living in Rio de Janeiro.

Back in the medieval times, people would have something called "first sleep" and "second sleep". They would go to sleep in the evening and would wake up around midnight. They would sleep among other people, including strangers. One of the activities that followed the first sleep was, of course, gossip.
